title: 9. Common Pitfalls to Avoid
use_cases: Use when a narrative spends excessive time on setting without introducing conflict
Implement when multiple plot twists overwhelm readers and dilute stakes
Configure when a climax fails to deliver a decisive emotional payoff
Apply when subplot threads are left unresolved and readers feel unsatisfied
content:
Being aware of these pitfalls helps you craft a tighter, more engaging narrative arc.

- Flat Exposition: Failing to hook readers early. Example: A story that spends too long describing the setting without introducing conflict can lose interest.
- Over‑packed Rising Action: Too many twists without clear stakes. Example: In a novel with 20 plot twists but no clear goal, readers may feel overwhelmed.
- Weak Climax: Lack of decisive moment or emotional payoff. Example: A climax that merely repeats the inciting incident offers little satisfaction.
- Unresolved Subplots: Leaving threads hanging without closure. Example: An unresolved love story can leave readers unsatisfied.
